The user wants to know what's technically possible for these visual effects. They are asking for a design feasibility discussion rather than immediate implementation.

The current collection shows unscanned badges as orange mystery boxes. The scan animation already displays the badge image immediately. The `isFirst` flag identifies new badge types. The required image assets are already available.

CSS blur filters and SVG lock overlays can create the locked badge effect. The blurred silhouette reveals colors and shapes as a tease. Labels will remain accessible for screen readers. Five badges at once is lightweight on mobile. The current orange mystery boxes would be replaced.

The existing ScanHit animation can be reused for this effect. The locked card would appear first. Then the lock shackle would open and rotate. A CSS blur transition would clear the background. CSS keyframes alone can handle the unlock animation without needing extra libraries. The effect should only trigger for first-of-type badges; repeat scans will skip the unlock and show the badge immediately. The sequence should last roughly 1.2 to 1.8 seconds so it does not block the user from tapping "Keep scanning." Autoplay can finish the unlock before revealing the call-to-action.

Reduced motion preferences should be respected by skipping the unlock animation entirely. The blur may reveal colors and spoil the mystery slightly, though heavier blur or keeping the question mark until unlock could mitigate this. The full-screen ScanHit overlay is the natural home for the unlock effects. A subtle echo glow on the collection card could reinforce the dopamine moment.

The collection card is too small in the horizontal scroller to carry a dramatic unlock. The full-screen ScanHit overlay is the better stage for the shackle animation and blur transition. The unlock should play directly on the scan success screen, using a card that resembles the collection slot. After the scan, the user lands back on the scanner rather than the collection, so the unlock belongs on the scan screen itself.

_**Agent (grok-4.7)**_

Both parts fit the app as it is. The collection already treats each badge as collected or locked, and a first scan of a new type is already flagged, so the unlock can play on the celebration screen that appears right after a scan.

**Locked badges in the collection**

Unscanned slots can show the real badge image, heavily blurred, with a lock centered on it and the label kept as `???`. The card stays the same size and shape as a collected badge. A strong blur still lets the orange, blue, and layout leak through, so the set looks like a teaser rather than a total mystery. CSS blur on five cards is cheap on a phone.

**Unlock after a new scan**

That moment belongs on the full-screen celebration that already plays after a successful scan (burst, bubbles, points). It only runs the first time that type is collected. A repeat of a type you already have skips it and shows the badge immediately.

A sequence that works well, about 1.5 seconds:

1. The same blurred card and lock appear, matching the collection.
2. The lock shackle lifts and snaps open, with a small flash and a scale punch.
3. The blur clears and the real badge is revealed.
4. The existing points and “first of this type” line land on top of that.

All of that can be CSS and an SVG lock, in the same style as the current pop and bubble effects. No new libraries.

When the player taps through, they return home and the collection already shows that badge sharp and unlocked. We can also give that card a short glow as they land, so the unlock connects back to the strip.

If someone has reduced motion turned on, the sequence should skip straight to the revealed badge. The app already respects that for other animations.

Specific CSS keyframes are being assigned to each unlock phase. The shackle rotates, the blur clears, the lock pops out, and the points fade up. Reduced motion will skip the entire sequence. A shine sweep may flash across the card. The lock SVG uses a rotating shackle path.

The lock SVG body and shackle paths are now defined. The shackle rotates around its bottom-right pivot and lifts upward. The CSS transform origin is set to 42px by 28px.

The shackle keyframe now lifts the lock eight pixels and rotates it twenty-eight degrees. The card will scale from 0.92 to 1.04 before settling. Extra sparkles and a white ring burst will surround the badge. Collection locked frames will layer a blurred image beneath a lock icon.

Considering accessibility for the locked badge teaser. Reconsidering the accessibility plan. The blurred image already reveals the badge type visually, so screen readers do not need a separate announcement. The shared BadgeLock component renders an SVG lock with a rotating shackle, body, and key. LockedBadge wraps the slot div and toggles between locked and unlocking states.

LockedBadge will keep the same image element throughout the reveal, animating its CSS filter instead of swapping images. The badge slot will layer a lock icon and a shine sweep over the blurred image. ScanHit will use a phase class on the badge reveal container to drive the unlock sequence.

The unlock sequence is now timed precisely. The locked phase lasts until 500 milliseconds, the opening phase until 1100 milliseconds, and the open phase begins immediately after. Users with reduced motion will start directly on the open state. A useEffect hook will manage the phase transitions.

The useEffect will only depend on `hit.isFirst` and `hit.type`, avoiding re-triggering from the phase state itself. A 420 millisecond timeout advances the badge from locked to opening, and another 1100 millisecond timeout advances it to open. The "Keep scanning" button will remain visible during the reveal so users can skip it, while the points number will pop in only once the badge fully opens.

A `freshBadge` state will carry the newly unlocked badge ID from the scan screen to the collection screen. Collection will apply a `just-got` class that triggers a single glow animation and then clears itself. The hit line will remain visible throughout the reveal.

The Home component will receive a `freshBadge` prop and an `onFreshSeen` callback to clear it once the glow finishes. Collection will run its `just-got` animation for 1.6 seconds before removing the class. Remounting Home via a React key ensures the animation plays fresh on every visit. Collection grid slots are styled with a fixed aspect ratio and relative positioning so the lock overlay layers cleanly without disrupting the mystery box layout.

Locked badge slots will scale the blurred image to 1.12 to hide blur edges. The lock overlay centers a 28% SVG lock with a dark blue translucent background and a soft drop shadow. Nested image styles need overriding to prevent conflicts with existing grid margins and aspect ratios.

Locked badges will blur at 14px and scale to 1.15, fading the blur and scale back to normal once the badge opens. The shackle rotates only during the opening and open phases. The lock icon then scales away, and a white flash sweeps across the card.

BadgeSlot will become a standalone component at src/components/BadgeSlot.tsx. It accepts src, alt, and a phase prop, rendering the lock overlay and shine sweep inside the badge slot. Collection and ScanHit will import this shared component to keep the lock markup consistent.

Collected badges will keep their plain image layout and skip the badge-slot wrapper entirely. The badge-slot wrapper is only used for locked badges. The lock icon will stay in the DOM during the entire unlock sequence so it can fade out naturally. _**Agent (grok-4.7)**_

Unscanned badges in the collection are now a blurred pass with a closed lock and `???`. The first time someone scans a new type, that same card unlocks on the celebration screen before the points land.

The unlock runs for about a second:

1. The blurred card shakes, like the lock is being tried.
2. The shackle lifts and swings open.
3. The blur clears, the lock pops away, and a flash, shine, and sparks reveal the badge.
4. The `+15` and “first of this type” line slam in.

A repeat of a badge you already have skips that and shows the pass immediately. When you leave the celebration, the new card in the collection glows briefly. If that scan also levels you up, the glow waits until you dismiss the level-up screen.

If reduced motion is on, the unlock is skipped and the badge appears straight away.
